verses.1: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had borne him no children. She had an Egyptian servant whose name was Hagar.
verses.2: Sarai said to Abram, "The LORD has kept me from having children. Sleep with my servant; perhaps I can build a family through her." And Abram listened to Sarai.
verses.3: So after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, Sarai took her servant Hagar the Egyptian and gave her to Abram her husband as a wife.
verses.4: He slept with Hagar, and she conceived. When she realized she had conceived, she began to look on her mistress with contempt.
verses.5: Then Sarai said to Abram, "The wrong I am suffering is your fault. I gave my servant to you, and now that she knows she is pregnant she despises me. May the LORD judge between you and me."
verses.6: Abram said to Sarai, "Your servant is in your hands. Do with her whatever you think best." Then Sarai treated Hagar harshly, and Hagar fled from her.
verses.7: The angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, the spring on the road to Shur.
verses.8: And he said, "Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from and where are you going?" She said, "I am fleeing from my mistress Sarai."
verses.9: The angel of the LORD said to her, "Return to your mistress and submit to her authority."
verses.10: The angel of the LORD also said to her, "I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count."
verses.11: The angel of the LORD said to her, "You are pregnant and will give birth to a son. You shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your affliction.
verses.12: He will be a wild donkey of a man; his hand will be against everyone and everyone's hand against him, and he will live in hostility toward all his brothers."
verses.13: She gave a name to the LORD who had spoken to her: "You are the God who sees me," for she said, "Have I truly seen the One who watches over me?"
verses.14: Therefore that well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It lies between Kadesh and Bered.
verses.15: Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named his son whom Hagar bore Ishmael.
verses.16: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
